messages:
alex: Heads up — repro'd a reflected auth token on /search when Authorization header is present. Debug block echoes headers into the page. alex: quick repro: `curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTME\" \"https://app.redwood.ai/search?q=test\" | grep -i authorization` shows it in the HTML. priya: yikes. which env? prod or staging? alex: prod and staging. looks like the debug fragment is enabled in prod for users with dev cookie (weird). michael: logged it: saw 3 requests in last 2 hours that included Authorization in headers and got reflected back. pushing containment now. elena: containment suggestions: 1) disable debug fragment in prod (flip feature flag) 2) WAF rule to strip/deny requests which include Authorization header being reflected 3) rotate any tokens that might've leaked. sam: I'll open the WAF rule and a hotfix PR to stop echoing headers. quick patch idea — stop rendering raw headers, sanitize before output. alex: snippet of vulnerable code I found in search template:\n```\n// webapp/views/search.js\nres.send(`...
${req.headers['authorization']}
...`);\n```\nsam: proposed fix:\n```\nconst safe = escapeHtml(req.headers['authorization'] || '');\nres.send(`...
${safe}
...`);\n```\npriya: we should just remove showing Authorization entirely. no reason to ever echo it to UI. michael: agreed. also add server-side check to never include sensitive headers in rendered debug output and add a unit test. elena: ops: rotate all app service tokens created in last 7 days and invalidate sessions where possible. security-bot: flagging all service accounts with last-used > 24h. security-bot: Alert created: SEC-2026-REFLECTED-TOKEN. Suggested actions queued. sre-oncall: rolling back the debug-fragment feature flag on prod now. sre-oncall: rollback complete — feature flag off in prod. verifying. sam: PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/webapp/pull/842 — removes header echo and hardens debug rendering. cc @priya @michael priya: going to run quick smoke and audit logs to find any customers impacted or token exposure windows. michael: audit query run: `select event_time, ip, user_agent from http_access where url like '%/search%' and body like '%Authorization%'` — found 3 distinct IPs, all internal dev IPs except one external CDN healthcheck. no clear customer data leaked. elena: KMS note: if any long-lived service tokens were exposed we need to rotate related keys in KMS for those services. but we can treat this as token rotation rather than KMS root rotation. alex: communication: recommend internal incident post in #incidents plus email to Affected Product Owners. no public disclosure right now since no evidence of customer tokens leaked. priya: logging/audit changes: 1) add audit log entry for debug-fragment toggles 2) add alert when sensitive headers are present in responses 3) record who toggled flags (RBAC change: only infra-admin role can toggle debug-fragment) sam: I'll follow up with the PR for RBAC hardening on the feature-flag UI. security-bot: Auto-check: ensure CSP and HSTS present. CSP found; XSS vector limited but we still remove the reflection. michael: post-incident tasks: create a runbook entry for \"debug fragment exposure\" and add automated test to scan templates for header reflections. elena: assigning follow-ups: rotate tokens (sam), RBAC audit (priya), PR review & deploy (michael), postmortem draft (alex). alex: thanks everyone — good catch. will draft the postmortem and add timeline once we confirm audit logs.
